gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states that Macworld timed the fan-cooled Anker MagGo 2 Pro at 30 minutes to 50% (33 minutes in Silent Mode) against 36 minutes for the fanless Baseus PicoGo AM52 on the same iPhone 16 Pro, or that Notebookcheck measured the AM52 peaking at 36.4 °C, about the 36 °C Anker claims for its fan-cooled pack.
standout_why: Compared against the cited Macworld roundup, Anker's 'Tested for Speed and Heat' blog and Anker's Qi2 25W page context. The Macworld roundup already carries the Recharge Test Scores (MagFlow Pro 208%, MagGo 2 Pro 199%, SnapGo Air 185%, AM52 182%) and the AM52's 36-minute figure, so that half is not new. In the part of the roundup I read (first 100,000 of 123,900 characters) it has no timing for the MagGo 2 Pro, no fan-on versus Silent Mode split, and no temperature readings. Anker's blog gives only Anker's own claims (50% in about 25 minutes on an iPhone 17 Pro, about 36 °C peak). Two cited pages could not be read: The Verge guide is blocked to the fetcher and the TechRadar UGREEN review returned only its title, so either could already hold timings or temperatures. PickedTech failed on a certificate error. The score is 2 rather than 3 because the finding confirms ChatGPT's pick instead of changing it.
decides: Confirms the Baseus PicoGo AM52 as the everyday pick and narrows the Anker's case. By Macworld's stopwatch the Anker's fan buys 6 minutes to 50% over the AM52 and only 3 minutes over the Anker's own Silent Mode, for $54 more at ChatGPT's $109.99 card price. Macworld's capacity test does favour the Anker (199% versus 182% of an iPhone). Notebookcheck's 36.4 °C peak on the fanless AM52 undercuts heat as a reason to pay for the fan, though its ambient temperature and instrument are not stated. One caution on the AM52: Macwelt saw its MagSafe 30-minute result swing between about 21% and 44% as the protection circuit cut power early. For the budget slot, Techlicious measured the INIU SnapGo Air at 30 to 32 Wh usable and never above 95 °F, but that is the $54.99 Air, which may not be the $44.99 'SnapGo Compact' ChatGPT showed.

findings.label: Hands-on charging results, weight and size (Cult of Mac, David Snow, published 2025-09-12)
findings.value: Wireless 50% to 100% in under two hours; wired 0 to about 35-40% in 30 min; 254 g; 110.8 × 70 × 21 mm

findings.note: Test phone iPhone 16 Pro. No temperature reading; the reviewer says it 'gets warm, but not alarmingly so'. The wireless figure covers the slow top half of the charge, so it is not comparable with the 0-50% times above. The review gives no model number; I matched it to ChatGPT's card by the 10,000 mAh capacity and 30 W built-in cable. At 254 g and 21 mm it is the heaviest and thickest of the candidates measured here.

findings.label: Usable energy, heat and recharge time (Techlicious, published 2026-10-02)
findings.value: About 30 to 32 Wh usable from a 39.2 Wh battery; surface never above 95 °F; recharge about 1 h 48 min
findings.note: Instruments: ChargerLAB POWER-Z KM003C, FNIRSI FNB58, infrared thermometer. 30/39.2 = 76.5% and 32/39.2 = 81.6%; Techlicious calls it about 80%. 95 °F is 35 °C. No wireless percent-in-minutes result. One 45 W wired run throttled to 24 W after 20 minutes. Techlicious lists $54.99, 7.1 oz and 0.5 in.

TechRadar's UGREEN MagFlow review (cited): the page returned only its title, so I could not read its charging-time or heat figures.
PickedTech's Qi2 power bank roundup: the fetch failed with a certificate error, so its contents were not compared.

Anker MagGo 2 Pro price at Anker's US store today: storecheck.py search on anker.com returned HTTP 404. ChatGPT's card and Macworld's roundup both show $109.99, but I did not confirm it at the maker's store.
Independent measurement of the Anker MagGo 2 Pro's surface temperature or fan noise in dB: Macworld's review has neither, and the Digital Camera World review returned only its title.
A measured 0-50% wireless time or temperature for the non-Pro UGREEN MagFlow 10000mAh with built-in cable: Cult of Mac gives only 50-100% and a subjective heat remark.

A measured wireless charging time for any INIU SnapGo model, and any named-reviewer measurement of the $44.99 'INIU SnapGo Compact' ChatGPT showed: every review found covers the SnapGo Air (P781), and I could not establish that the two are the same product.
RTINGS, SoundGuys, ChargerLAB or Wirecutter measurements for these Qi2.2 power banks: the searches surfaced none, and I did not run a dedicated search for each.
Ambient temperature and instrument behind Notebookcheck's 36.4 °C reading: the review states neither.
